scope: Object-near census of 1844-1845 Hodgson/British Museum reconciliation devices reconstructed from ZSL digital archive records.

core_concept.definition: A list, table, catalogue, receipt or annotated copy on which expected and observed collection states can be compared, exceptions recorded, and a corrected or synchronized state requested or propagated.

states_compared: later prose count within same copy
records.interpretive_warning: The surviving witness is a copy. Do not infer that the dispatched original contained the same inconsistency.
records.article_value: Arithmetic reveals incompatible count states inside the archival witness itself.

records.direct_mechanism: Hodgson states numbered catalogues provide a ready clue to how many drawings ought to be forthcoming.
records.warning: Species count is not drawing count; Hodgson states many species had several delineations.

records.downstream_action: destination letters and physical duplicate distribution
records.article_value: Hodgson explicitly requests a three-state institutional reconciliation before completing distribution.

records.global_scope: all birds and mammals discovered by Hodgson in Nepal
records.article_value: Distributed specimen set is mapped onto a global descriptive universe by an explicit graphical subset marker.

records.correction_event: Hodgson requests a copy when corrected and offers to pay for copying.
records.article_value: A tabular institutional account becomes a negotiated correction surface rather than final metadata.

records.identifier_function: numbers on osteological remains refer to skin/drawing series and allow species identification
records.warning: Species-level linkage does not automatically prove same biological individual across representations.
records.article_value: Direct statement that numbering bridges physically separated media.

records.problem: Indian publications containing Hodgson descriptions were rare in London and scarcer on the Continent.
catalogue_functions: prevent names being treated as mere manuscript names
records.article_value: Institutional legibility includes bibliographic synchronization, not only object labels.
Corrected metadata version is designed to travel with physical duplicates.
Duplicate/distributed status does not entail low evidentiary standing.

cross_record_rules: Expected-state counts and observed-state counts must be stored separately.
A surviving copy can contain a count conflict without proving that the dispatched original did.
Global catalogue scope and destination physical subset must be represented as separate layers.
Graphical subset markers such as crosses, ticks, underlining or destination initials are first-class metadata.
Received, retained and distributed are distinct collection states.
A corrected catalogue can be part of the physical distribution protocol itself.
Identifiers can support object, relational or historical-event addressability at different evidential strengths.
Duplicate is an operational/distribution status and does not automatically determine evidentiary rank.
